findings.where: Screen 1 readout row 'C × steepness: 318 µF × 31,416 V/s ≈ 10.00 A'; screen 6 row 'X_C = 1 ÷ (2π × 60 × 0.000318) ≈ 8.33 Ω' and its Why? ('the same as')
findings.what: Worked by hand with C as written, these give 9.99 A and 8.34 Ω, not the 10.00 A and 8.33 Ω shown, because C is really 318.3 µF; write C as 318.3 µF / 0.0003183 F (which gives 10.00 A and 8.333 Ω), or show the current to one decimal place.

'A healthy capacitor reads like this, so it is not open-circuit' does not follow, because an open-circuit capacitor also reads very high; say that an open one would pass nothing on 50 Hz either, yet this one passes 10 A peak, and that a reading that climbs, rather than sitting high from the start, shows the plates filling.
